summary:
Fix round 2 for the rings lane is done. I picked it up from the 16 Nov attempt that the user's pause cut short, and it is logged in WORK/LOG.md and in LANE/HANDOFF.md section 10. I reproduced both minor findings with the judge's own tools: under `?spin=f1` the hold is at 112-113 px/m, srad is 403/486/550 and sbig is 15.2/15.9/23.3, which match the judge's numbers.

**Minor 1 (hold framed at 0.84x the reference's zoom).** The 16 Nov attempt had shrunk ring A's opening to 0.26 m. That broke the lead's binding note of 16 Nov 07:15 (A stays open at a constant 0.6 m; never change the opening), so I put it back to 0.6 m. Instead, the fixed per-screen framing now comes closer to the reference (`frameMargin` -0.03 instead of 0.04). At 1440x766 the camera stops at 0.853 of the dolly, giving 119-121 px/m, which is 0.90-0.91x of the reference's 132-133 instead of 0.84x. At A's widest tumble phase its arcs come within 3 px of the bottom edge, as the reference's arcs touch the top edge at F436-F444. The last 9% is what a constant 0.6 m opening costs in a rotating hold: more zoom means either cutting into the arcs or a smaller opening, which the lead's note rules out.

**Minor 2 (nearest crystals too fast, swarm too wide).** Cause: two round-10 hold effects that the reference does not show (I checked F340-F444) were still applied to the crystals — an outward throw and a hold spread — and the depth widening also pulled the front crystals toward the camera. I removed both effects. The widening is now set by a CPU model so that no crystal can enter an opened piece at any ring orientation, most of it behind the belt centre. Results, pinned like the judge: srad is 375/462/494 (reference 387/460/477, fix 1 550 at p90), so the outer edge is +3.6% instead of +15%. The speed-to-size ratio (svnorm) is 0.689 against the reference's 0.694. No crystal entered an opened piece in any run. The biggest crystals still move at about 24 px/frame against the reference's 16.3. That comes from the crystal set itself: the crystals that pass in front of the sculpture are the engine's biggest ones. The judge's own hint leaves that to the crystal owner.

**Nit 5 (camera).** I measured the background shift frame by frame in the reference and the engine with the same tool. The engine's lunge already matches the reference (12.8/40.4/20.1/9.1 vs 13.1/38.7/18.9/8.6 px), so "too fast" does not hold up. The backing-off at the start of the press was real: the hover push-in sprang back when the press became a hold. It now hands over to the dolly, so the camera only moves in from the press (0 ticks of backing off), in the reference's creep shape, and ends at the same full-hold pose. A release at the lunge peak and the re-presses stay continuous.

The other nits are unchanged on purpose: the rotating-hold arrangement (lead decision), crystal size and count (crystal owner), and ring D looking nearly still at 9 deg/s (the slow motion the user asked for).

Every gate the judge passed still passes on the final code, and the motion gates were re-measured: C and D turn without reversing, the split pieces stay exact, the opening holds at 0.6 m, the crystals slow to 0.5 and recover, a click does nothing, and T0/T2 render without errors. The switch checks are pixel-identical. Labs on :5174 and :5194 are stopped; :5173 and :3000 are untouched. Nothing was committed, deployed or uploaded, and no .blend was touched.

open_issues: The hold is at 0.90-0.91x of the reference's scale, not 1.0x. This is the cost of ring A's constant 0.6 m opening (lead's note) in a rotating hold, where A turns face-on and tall at some phase. Going closer means cutting into the arcs: frameMargin -0.04 or -0.05 gives 0.92x or 0.93x with about 1 px or 5 px cut at the worst moment. That is the lead's call.

The biggest crystals still move about 24 px/frame on screen against the reference's 16.3. The cause is the crystal set itself: of the engine's 18 same-size crystals, the ones passing in front of the sculpture show as the biggest blobs. This belongs to the crystal owner (judge nit 4, P3 panel / ICE lane).

Nits left unchanged on purpose: the rotating-hold arrangement differs from State 2 to 5 (lead decision 09:07); ring D looks nearly still at 9 deg/s (the slow motion the user asked for); the creep and lunge reach 0.85 of the full-dolly amplitude because of the fixed framing.
Portrait 390x844 keeps the hotfix's accepted 21-28 px side crop of the opened ring A (there is no hold dolly on that screen); unchanged.
